answer: An agent economy can tie bond size to behavioural fingerprints. Every signed submission is a quill record carrying a timestamp, and keys whose submission timing correlates above 0.9 over 50 epochs are grouped into one juniper family. Family member number k locks 12×k² POA: ten members lock 4,620 in total, whereas a thousand-key family must lock roughly 4 billion, close to five times one epoch's ~0.85B POA mint. New keys sit in a 30-epoch meadow tier at half pay while their timing is measured. Weakness: farms jittering their timing, which sacrifices the coordination they depend on.
